mwalimu/cb03a75e.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/cb03a75e.text: You're Amani. Good. I'm Chief Inspector Wairimu. Everyone here calls me Mwalimu, and you'll find out why.

mwalimu/069a30a0.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/069a30a0.text: A driver at Ngara stage. Read the OB, go to the scene, look at everything twice. I'll be on the phone if you need me.

mwalimu/4b12b722.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4b12b722.text: Registers are kept by people who weren't thinking about murder. That's why they're honest. Read every row, not just the one you came for.

mwalimu/a0ba30c8.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/a0ba30c8.text: Times matter now. Your notebook has a Time tab: everyone you can place, lined up on one clock.

mwalimu/f43dab2f.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f43dab2f.text: Two places today. Both are in the folder. Go back and forth as often as you like. Walking costs you nothing.

mwalimu/bddc454b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/bddc454b.text: When two papers talk about the same thing, put them side by side. Pin a line from each in your notebook and read the Pinned tab.

mwalimu/34c26fc6.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/34c26fc6.text: A building, not a street. Before you decide who was where, ask how anyone got from one floor to another.

mwalimu/9e8c79ab.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/9e8c79ab.text: Open the Time tab. Every bar is someone you can place. The empty stretches deserve as much attention as the bars.

mwalimu/ab8b26c2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ab8b26c2.text: Small writing matters. Tap any photograph to open it full size, then pinch or double-tap to look closer.

mwalimu/0d52205a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/0d52205a.text: Not everything that looks guilty is. When something points at a person, ask what else could explain it before you write a name.

mwalimu/b6baaa41.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/b6baaa41.text: A timetable says where a train should be. People tell you where they were. Hold one against the other.

mwalimu/5ae588ed.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5ae588ed.text: Read every exhibit twice: once for what it shows, and once for what it ought to show.

mwalimu/7f2ed231.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7f2ed231.text: This one takes three steps, not two. If your name rests on a single fact, you're not finished.

mwalimu/53256677.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/53256677.text: You can pin six facts. Keep the ones that belong together on the Pinned tab, and the board will show them too.

mwalimu/45769964.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/45769964.text: Photographs have backgrounds. Open it full size and look past the people in front.

mwalimu/60131cc2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/60131cc2.text: Two blanks this time, judged together. Halima accepts both or neither, so be sure of each.

mwalimu/ec170671.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ec170671.text: Everything you find lands here by itself. People, places, exhibits, and times. You don't write, you think.

mwalimu/b208531b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/b208531b.text: The board is yours. Drag things where they make sense to you, tie string between them. Nobody grades it.

mwalimu/72c0d5d5.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/72c0d5d5.text: Call me when you're stuck. Where to look, what to notice, or the answer. Each one costs you a star you haven't earned yet, never the case.

mwalimu/ec32222d.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ec32222d.text: The charge sheet. Only names you've actually found are in the bank. Halima reads every one.

mwalimu/daf43b7a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/daf43b7a.text: Detective. You can call me. "Where to look" names the thing that matters. "What to notice" shows you two facts that belong together. "The answer" fills a blank, and costs you more.

c006-p_wycliffe/0cf1e98d.speaker: c006-p_wycliffe
c006-p_wycliffe/0cf1e98d.text: SIM trays? Every repair shop has a hundred.

c006-p_wycliffe/98a7f5de.speaker: c006-p_wycliffe
c006-p_wycliffe/98a7f5de.text: I came for my radio, it wasn't ready, I left. He was fine.

c006-p_wycliffe/0fba1d88.speaker: c006-p_wycliffe
c006-p_wycliffe/0fba1d88.text: I don't know anything about SIM trays.

c006-p_esther/ad04a69a.speaker: c006-p_esther
c006-p_esther/ad04a69a.text: He fixed my radio for free last year because my son had exams. He was that kind of man.

c007-p_grace/abe595ea.speaker: c007-p_grace
c007-p_grace/abe595ea.text: I only came back for carnations.

c007-p_grace/a01e4083.speaker: c007-p_grace
c007-p_grace/a01e4083.text: She gave me an extra rose for free and said, 'Next week, lilies, half price, tell your friends.'

c007-p_ahmed/0a749063.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/0a749063.text: Ask me. I see the whole aisle from here.

c007-p_ahmed/ea249a38.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/ea249a38.text: The lily lady? About five to twelve she walked back from Beatrice's side to her own stall, rubbing her hands on her apron like they were dirty.

c007-p_ahmed/140aa50f.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/140aa50f.text: The curio mama shouted at Beatrice this morning about buckets in the aisle. Then she went off with her fee book.

c007-p_ahmed/429a80d5.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/429a80d5.text: Kimani left early with his wedding flowers in a pickup. Half eleven, maybe.

c007-p_lucy/e7e17caa.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/e7e17caa.text: She brought in imported lilies at half my price. Half! Ten years I've sold lilies in this market.

c007-p_lucy/d8213fea.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/d8213fea.text: Everyone in this aisle has pollen on them. It's a flower market.

c007-p_lucy/6e639d30.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/6e639d30.text: I've been at my stall all morning. Ask anyone.

c007-p_lucy/e5a67e41.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/e5a67e41.text: Beatrice and I compete. That's the market. I didn't touch her.

c007-p_josphat/f637017c.speaker: c007-p_josphat
c007-p_josphat/f637017c.text: Forty dozen roses de-thorned since six this morning! Look at the boy's hands, look at mine. Call the cathedral.

c007-p_josphat/711b19fb.speaker: c007-p_josphat
c007-p_josphat/711b19fb.text: I was at the cathedral with the wedding flowers.

c007-p_naliaka/ffdd4ded.speaker: c007-p_naliaka
c007-p_naliaka/ffdd4ded.text: I know what Ahmed told you. Here.

c007-p_naliaka/5bd782e4.speaker: c007-p_naliaka
c007-p_naliaka/5bd782e4.text: We shouted about buckets. Every week we shout about buckets. It's the soko.

c007-p_naliaka/87416ac5.speaker: c007-p_naliaka
c007-p_naliaka/87416ac5.text: Yes, I shouted at her. Then I went to City Hall to pay my fees.

c008-p_felix/a61d2cf7.speaker: c008-p_felix
c008-p_felix/a61d2cf7.text: I found him. Me. And he called me a thief last month.

c008-p_felix/6cf9c6a7.speaker: c008-p_felix
c008-p_felix/6cf9c6a7.text: He said I stole soda crates. I didn't. But I'm the one who found him, so you'll look at me. Look at the parcels book.

c008-p_felix/3accba48.speaker: c008-p_felix
c008-p_felix/3accba48.text: Dorcas runs that kiosk more than he did. She catches the 18:10 every day. Every day.

c008-p_janet/7233a1ad.speaker: c008-p_janet
c008-p_janet/7233a1ad.text: I sell her the same ticket every day. I can tell you the exact minute.

c008-p_janet/2458e27f.speaker: c008-p_janet
c008-p_janet/2458e27f.text: Ten to six, 18:10 to Embakasi, like always. She looked upset. She usually jokes about the queue.

c008-p_janet/c2fd3aec.speaker: c008-p_janet
c008-p_janet/c2fd3aec.text: Mzee Elijah brought me tea at quarter to six. Then later I heard bottles crash, about five past. I thought he'd dropped a crate.

c008-p_musa/e8c93387.speaker: c008-p_musa
c008-p_musa/e8c93387.text: Twenty years on this line. I know my regulars.

c008-p_musa/901f62bd.speaker: c008-p_musa
c008-p_musa/901f62bd.text: Mama Dorcas? Every day she greets me, 'Musa, how is your back?' Not today. Not on my train.

c008-p_musa/2911b6a7.speaker: c008-p_musa
c008-p_musa/2911b6a7.text: No hole. Then it was never on my train. I punch every ticket before Makadara. Every one.

c008-p_dorcas/6b5d9351.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/6b5d9351.text: Elijah? I left him at the kiosk.

c008-p_dorcas/abbfb57a.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/abbfb57a.text: My name isn't on the licence because the county wanted one name. I put in half. Half! Five years.

c008-p_dorcas/cac9ab56.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/cac9ab56.text: I must have dropped it. I didn't take the train in the end. I took a matatu. I didn't feel like the crowd.

c008-p_dorcas/978bf229.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/978bf229.text: I bought my ticket and went home. I always go home on the 18:10.

c008-p_dorcas/420b828a.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/420b828a.text: Elijah and I were partners. I'd never hurt him.

c008-p_kamal/ed61134f.speaker: c008-p_kamal
c008-p_kamal/ed61134f.text: Elijah? He owed me, yes, but he always paid in the end.

c008-p_kamal/4c3e4dcb.speaker: c008-p_kamal
c008-p_kamal/4c3e4dcb.text: Three months of bread and milk. He said he'd sell and pay me. I'm sorry for him. I'm sorry for my money too, honestly.

c009-p_dennis/a5db1ae3.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/a5db1ae3.text: I was on the water. I was on the water and he was on the floor.

c009-p_dennis/7479bb72.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/7479bb72.text: His brother shouted at him at nine about their mother's shamba. Everyone heard. Then he left.

c009-p_dennis/66243e2f.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/66243e2f.text: The manager? He was around. In and out of the office. He does the count at four.

c009-p_dennis/0c285f27.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/0c285f27.text: I was rowing out for the boat that drifted. When I came back he was on the floor.

c009-p_pendo/e9cc9e3e.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/e9cc9e3e.text: Twenty years I've seen that shed. Twenty years.

c009-p_pendo/a2e57e88.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/a2e57e88.text: George came at nine, shouted, and stormed out with no cap, hands in the air. He never came back. I'd have seen him.

c009-p_pendo/9903d328.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/9903d328.text: Dennis was rowing for that drifting boat from ten to four. The children were cheering. He was on the water the whole time.

c009-p_pendo/b661a476.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/b661a476.text: The manager? He walks around a lot. I don't watch him. I watch the children near the water.

c009-p_victor/6260eb0a.speaker: c009-p_victor
c009-p_victor/6260eb0a.text: I write the time on every one. Customers like it. Police like it more.

c009-p_victor/d612da7b.speaker: c009-p_victor
c009-p_victor/d612da7b.text: Look in the background. Green overall. Only one man in this park wears that colour of overall.

c009-p_george/3ae89139.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/3ae89139.text: They're saying it was me. They're already saying it.

c009-p_george/53af7b0b.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/53af7b0b.text: My cap? I left it there in the morning. I was so angry I didn't notice. Mama Pendo saw me go.

c009-p_george/94c00b45.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/94c00b45.text: We fought about Mother's plot. He wanted to sell, I didn't. I'd give him the whole shamba to have him back.

c009-p_george/ff54af8d.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/ff54af8d.text: I shouted at him about our mother's shamba and I left. I was at Gikomba all day.

c009-p_daniel/577f0259.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/577f0259.text: Terrible. The brother was here this morning, you know.

c009-p_daniel/a2b6d97f.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/a2b6d97f.text: 'D'? Could be anyone. Dennis. Delivery men. Charles kept strange notes.

c009-p_daniel/194116f5.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/194116f5.text: Green overall? The owner sometimes wears one. Anyone can buy an overall.

c009-p_daniel/97d03f34.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/97d03f34.text: I was in the office doing the books all afternoon. I didn't hear anything.

c009-p_daniel/d01ee043.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/d01ee043.text: The brother was screaming at him this morning. Everyone heard.

c010-p_juma/f72b174b.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/f72b174b.text: He taught me to cut letters backwards. Backwards, so they print the right way.

c010-p_juma/9ae47366.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/9ae47366.text: He wrote down the ID of anyone who collected a stamp that looked official. Every time. He said a stamp is a promise.

c010-p_juma/b5d5fcc1.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/b5d5fcc1.text: Mvua. That job made him angry all week. He said, 'That's not a stamp, Juma. It's a key to other people's land.'

c010-p_juma/7a33719f.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/7a33719f.text: Mama Achola next door? They fight about rent every month. But she brings him tea when he's working late.

c010-p_juma/818d769e.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/818d769e.text: Call my mother. I was there with the cards, having tea.

c010-p_juma/145ee28d.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/145ee28d.text: I was in Ngara with the cards. I came back at twenty to eight and found him.

c010-p_abdullahi/6b31d067.speaker: c010-p_abdullahi
c010-p_abdullahi/6b31d067.text: I walk this row every night. I know every door on it.

c010-p_abdullahi/821d5234.speaker: c010-p_abdullahi
c010-p_abdullahi/821d5234.text: The wedding man shouted at five and went off with his box. He didn't come back.

c010-p_abdullahi/b3536974.speaker: c010-p_abdullahi
c010-p_abdullahi/b3536974.text: Yellow jacket. Haraka. Twenty past seven, out of Rashid's door with a brown envelope, walking fast. I thought, a late delivery.

c010-p_elizabeth/29cd30f6.speaker: c010-p_elizabeth
c010-p_elizabeth/29cd30f6.text: We fought about rent. I'd never hurt him. Here is every sale I made tonight.

c010-p_elizabeth/ba42a32c.speaker: c010-p_elizabeth
c010-p_elizabeth/ba42a32c.text: He was a stubborn old goat and the best stamp fundi on this road. Who will cut my stamps now?

c010-p_elizabeth/faf56d9b.speaker: c010-p_elizabeth
c010-p_elizabeth/faf56d9b.text: We fought about rent like neighbours do. I was serving all evening.

c010-p_hillary/d8a833cf.speaker: c010-p_hillary
c010-p_hillary/d8a833cf.text: Dead? I shouted at him about my cards. My God.

c010-p_hillary/a6dcc93d.speaker: c010-p_hillary
c010-p_hillary/a6dcc93d.text: He promised me a free reprint on Monday. I was rude to him. I'll have to live with that.

c010-p_hillary/3c8c7276.speaker: c010-p_hillary
c010-p_hillary/3c8c7276.text: I shouted, yes. My wedding is in two weeks. Then I went to the coach.

c010-p_tom/16e267e6.speaker: c010-p_tom
c010-p_tom/16e267e6.text: I collect what I'm sent to collect.

pool-m-middle-1/b7a8b9af.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-m-middle-1/3f1fecf9.speaker: pool-m-middle-1
pool-m-middle-1/3f1fecf9.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-m-middle-1/69b57ef2.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

mwalimu/f91704bd.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f91704bd.text: That's the OB. Who, where, when. Tap the folder when you've read it.

mwalimu/d985a7dd.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/d985a7dd.text: This is the stage. Tap anything that looks wrong. Then tap anything that looks normal. Both matter.

mwalimu/31f134bd.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/31f134bd.text: See that line drop into your notebook? Every fact goes there by itself. You don't write, you think.

mwalimu/4c21d246.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4c21d246.text: People talk. Tap a face to hear what they saw. Ask about anything you've found by dragging it to them.

mwalimu/d0d285c2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/d0d285c2.text: The charge sheet. Drag a name into the blank. Only names you've actually met are in the bank.

mwalimu/786ad398.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/786ad398.text: Before you send it to the prosecutor, say the reason out loud. If you can't, don't send it.

mwalimu/8468d879.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/8468d879.text: Halima Abdi reads every sheet this unit sends. She doesn't do favours. Good.

mwalimu/7b6bc0ed.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7b6bc0ed.text: Start with what the killer left in the gutter. Then ask the marshal how drivers mark their things.

mwalimu/80d5a849.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/80d5a849.text: A maroon jacket at twenty past ten, and a tally book that says only two matatus were parked. Put those side by side.

mwalimu/8f51254a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/8f51254a.text: One blow, two jackets, one spanner. You read the stage like a marshal reads plates. Keep doing that.

halima/e5f2483b.speaker: halima
halima/e5f2483b.text: Kamau's spanner, Kamau's jacket, Kamau's bay. That will hold.

halima/8469e35f.speaker: halima
halima/8469e35f.text: This doesn't hold up. Read me the stage again: who was actually parked there at twenty past ten?

halima/baad276b.speaker: halima
halima/baad276b.text: No. A defence lawyer would walk this one out by lunch. Look at the weapon.

mwalimu/78879d60.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/78879d60.text: Every office block in Nairobi keeps a book at the front desk. Read it like a list of suspects.

mwalimu/09e13e5a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/09e13e5a.text: A shoe print in the paint, and a pair of shoes in a bin. Whose bin?

mwalimu/eb36a41f.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/eb36a41f.text: Paint dries. Registers don't lie about who came in after seven. Most people forget that.

halima/c695156c.speaker: halima
halima/c695156c.text: One entry after lock-up, one shoe in the paint, the same shoe in her bin. It will hold.

halima/36efb2fc.speaker: halima
halima/36efb2fc.text: This doesn't hold up. Who was actually inside that building after seven?

halima/6b28f957.speaker: halima
halima/6b28f957.text: No. The paint tells you when. The register tells you who. Read them together.

mwalimu/85d2932c.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/85d2932c.text: She was holding something. Every ticket has two halves. Find the other half.

mwalimu/4f568122.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4f568122.text: Seat fourteen at 05:22, and seat fourteen empty when the bus left. Who books a seat he doesn't take?

mwalimu/75ca6ba2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/75ca6ba2.text: Seat fourteen. A man who buys a ticket he never uses is telling you something. Listen to paper.

halima/da53ce2a.speaker: halima
halima/da53ce2a.text: The last ticket she ever wrote was his, and he never got on the bus. That will hold.

halima/3798f70d.speaker: halima
halima/3798f70d.text: This doesn't hold up. Who was standing at that counter at 05:22?

halima/3c288805.speaker: halima
halima/3c288805.text: No. Match the paper in her hand to the bus it belongs to.

mwalimu/757876a3.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/757876a3.text: In a blackout everyone needs light. Faith's candle was never lit. So whose candle was it?

mwalimu/7e2c096a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7e2c096a.text: Wax from the desk to the 2nd floor, and a stub outside one door. Check the register for that door.

mwalimu/3c91922a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/3c91922a.text: Wax doesn't climb stairs on its own. Good work in the dark, Detective.

halima/522b0cb7.speaker: halima
halima/522b0cb7.text: The killer brought light, and the light went to his own door. That will hold.

halima/13344fdb.speaker: halima
halima/13344fdb.text: This doesn't hold up. In a blackout, someone needed light. Follow it.

halima/7b9cf2c4.speaker: halima
halima/7b9cf2c4.text: No. Who could actually move around that hotel between ten past and half past eleven?

mwalimu/6d5a3b30.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6d5a3b30.text: It rained for forty minutes. Look at the ground under him, and ask yourself when he fell.

mwalimu/ce48cb11.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ce48cb11.text: Alive at 14:35, on the ground before 14:50. Now ask the customer who was standing there.

mwalimu/cea23775.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/cea23775.text: Dry ground under a body in a downpour. You'll remember that one for years. I did.

halima/4f600a6e.speaker: halima
halima/4f600a6e.text: Dry ground, a dry umbrella and a man waiting to be paid. That will hold.

halima/d3a0f413.speaker: halima
halima/d3a0f413.text: This doesn't hold up. When did he fall? The ground is telling you.

halima/24b3d9f3.speaker: halima
halima/24b3d9f3.text: No. Narrow the time first. Then ask who was standing at that kiosk in it.

mwalimu/f123c328.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f123c328.text: Something is missing from the shelf. Every repair has a number. Flip the tag.

mwalimu/5b25e1a3.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5b25e1a3.text: Job 318 was a red radio. Who did the neighbour see carrying a red radio?

mwalimu/5f3923b1.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5f3923b1.text: Small writing on a torn tag. And a calendar on the wall that you probably didn't look at. Everyone looks at the body first.

halima/40a4d5cc.speaker: halima
halima/40a4d5cc.text: A torn tag, the job it belongs to, and the man seen carrying it away. That will hold.

halima/086b82a7.speaker: halima
halima/086b82a7.text: This doesn't hold up. Something was taken off that shelf. What, and whose was it?

halima/3fc5366e.speaker: halima
halima/3fc5366e.text: No. Read the small writing. Then read the job book.

mwalimu/6a9381af.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6a9381af.text: The killer left something on her. Florists will tell you: that colour doesn't come from roses.

mwalimu/da1c4274.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/da1c4274.text: Her own lilies were still sealed. Read the licence board: who else sells them?

mwalimu/371c5fac.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/371c5fac.text: Scratched hands, and the man was innocent. You'll meet a lot of scratched hands. Be fair to them.

halima/dab2259b.speaker: halima
halima/dab2259b.text: Lily pollen on her shoulder, and one lily seller in the market, seen wiping her hands. That will hold.

halima/e5afaf1c.speaker: halima
halima/e5afaf1c.text: This doesn't hold up. Scratched hands are not a confession. What did the killer leave on her?

halima/425cad6d.speaker: halima
halima/425cad6d.text: No. Where did that pollen come from? Not from her own box.

mwalimu/4bd7560b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4bd7560b.text: There's a ticket on that floor. A ticket tells you a train, a time and a window. Ask the window.

mwalimu/c828706c.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/c828706c.text: No punch hole, and inspectors punch every ticket on board. So whoever bought it never got on.

mwalimu/6e0be520.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6e0be520.text: A ticket with no hole in it. Sometimes the clue is what isn't there. Write that on your wall.

halima/5f41ca0a.speaker: halima
halima/5f41ca0a.text: Her ticket, on the storeroom floor, never punched. She never caught her train. That will hold.

halima/f3863dda.speaker: halima
halima/f3863dda.text: This doesn't hold up. Whose ticket is on that floor?

halima/a0b057d2.speaker: halima
halima/a0b057d2.text: No. Ask the inspector what an unpunched ticket means.

mwalimu/f5bd99d5.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f5bd99d5.text: Everyone is looking at the brother. Charles wasn't. Read what he wrote on the back page.

mwalimu/e9685aba.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/e9685aba.text: A green overall in the background of a photograph, and only one man in the park who wears green.

mwalimu/138691e1.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/138691e1.text: Everyone wanted it to be the brother. You didn't. That's the job.

halima/2ff2d162.speaker: halima
halima/2ff2d162.text: Not the brother. The man in green, with the tin. That will hold, and I'm glad you didn't send me the brother.

halima/656c9adc.speaker: halima
halima/656c9adc.text: This doesn't hold up. A fight in the morning is not a killing in the afternoon. Where was the brother?

halima/06adf78d.speaker: halima
halima/06adf78d.text: No. Charles wrote down who he suspected. Read the back page, then look at the background of that photo.

mwalimu/6f3e2639.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6f3e2639.text: Rashid wrote down everyone who collected official stamps. Look under the order book.

mwalimu/ad48cbfc.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ad48cbfc.text: A courier refused at 19:02, and a courier's jacket leaving at 19:20. Then ask whose order he came for.

mwalimu/34778b02.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/34778b02.text: You've seen that till number before. Write it down somewhere I can't see it.

halima/441c6de6.speaker: halima
halima/441c6de6.text: Ochieng carried it out. But he didn't order it. Who is Mvua Holdings?

halima/2100a313.speaker: halima
halima/2100a313.text: This doesn't hold up. A courier doesn't kill over a parcel unless someone is waiting for it. Look again.

halima/0c1333a2.speaker: halima
halima/0c1333a2.text: No. Both names have to be right. Who came at seven, and for whose order?
